page: Microsoft Azure FX64mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 1344.0 GB of RAM, yielding 21.0 GB of memory per core, alongside 3780 GB of local storage.

Benchmark evaluations position this server in the top 10% for memory bandwidth, recording read-only large block speeds of 392.4 GB/sec and write large block speeds of 170.98 GB/sec. Passmark database operations also rank in the top 10% with a score of 37190.82, and static web serving throughput reaches 97.07 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25%, while single-core CPU performance falls into the middle 50% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX64mds_v2 offers high resource density, particularly regarding its memory-to-vCPU ratio and large local storage capacity. The hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, though the average single-core CPU performance represents a tradeoff for tasks that cannot leverage parallel processing or the massive memory bandwidth.

This server is configured for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database operations, in-memory caching platforms like Redis, and data-heavy web serving. It is also capable of handling medium-scale LLM inference workloads, achieving 292.5 tokens/sec for prompt processing on 7B models.
